scope: Exhaustive current macro-branch membership review: all six continents, 29 subcontinents, 66 regions and 487 member areas enumerated. This is a source-backed diagnostic pass, not completion of lower-tier semantic research.

source_assessment.wgsrpd: WGSRPD is a botanical recording scheme. Its introduction explicitly states most regions were specially circumscribed and boundaries may follow political provinces. PDF reasoning was inspected, including Azores phytogeographic placement, all-Kazakhstan political integrity, Malesia/Papuasia and island associations. It supplies candidates, not semantic approval.
source_assessment.un_m49: M49 is a statistical country/area scheme, not physical boundary geometry. Used to corroborate recognized Pacific subregion roles; not used to assign continental land or all islands of a transoceanic owner.
source_assessment.continent_convention: National Geographic provides broad continent/island associations and Ural division. Detailed Caucasus/Aegean/Azores ambiguity is corroborated by inspected secondary overview; choosing an exact boundary still requires a named atlas convention and source geometry.

continents.name: Africa
continents.assessment: Mainland role is recognizable; explicit boundaries must address Sinai/Suez, Socotra, Macaronesia/Azores, overseas enclaves and remote Atlantic/Indian islands. Botanical Africa is not automatically the physical six-continent convention.

continents.name: Asia
continents.assessment: Ural/Caucasus/Aegean boundaries and Southeast-Asia/Oceania archipelago division require a stated physical convention. Whole Kazakhstan and North Caucasus botanical placement cannot be described as an audited watershed boundary.

continents.name: Europe
continents.assessment: Review Ural/Caucasus transitions, Aegean islands and Azores convention; Western/Central/Northern labels are atlas choices. Crown Dependencies currently reveal regional misassignments rather than continent errors.

continents.name: North America
continents.assessment: Mainland plus Caribbean/Greenland is defensible, all Mexico is retained. Audit Bermuda, Clipperton, Bimini and Canadian/French offshore islands under explicit geographic association independent of owner.

continents.name: Oceania
continents.assessment: Expanded Oceania is a stated association for Australasia and Pacific islands. Pacific subcontinent membership currently contains real errors; Antarctic-excluded southern islands need a separate explicit association policy.

continents.name: South America
continents.assessment: Isthmus boundary at Panama/Colombia and associated east-Pacific/south-Atlantic archipelagos are geographic conventions. Whole-country western/eastern subdivision needs justification rather than inference from current ownership.

subcontinents.name: Andean South America
subcontinents.assessment: Current whole-country territories include extensive non-Andean land; name/purpose requires correction or broader convention.

subcontinents.name: Atlantic Islands
subcontinents.assessment: Noncontiguous archipelagos; association policy and subantarctic exceptions remain open.

subcontinents.name: Australasia
subcontinents.assessment: Australia/New Zealand/associated islands convention; Cocos/Christmas and subantarctic associations remain open.

subcontinents.name: Caribbean
subcontinents.assessment: Bermuda and Bahamian outliers require explicit Atlantic/Caribbean association, separate from ownership.

subcontinents.name: Central Africa
subcontinents.assessment: Congo Basin versus African Great Lakes transition; political source units are not a full basin partition.

subcontinents.name: Central Asia
subcontinents.assessment: All Kazakhstan membership is a source convention; region duplicates the whole subcontinent.

subcontinents.name: Eastern Africa
subcontinents.assessment: Includes broad botanical northeast/Horn/Sahel; Chad/Sudan require explicit regional convention.

subcontinents.name: Eastern Asia
subcontinents.assessment: Japan/China/Mongolia/Korea/Taiwan memberships are present, but legacy residual China/Eastern Asia groups need repair.

subcontinents.name: Eastern Europe
subcontinents.assessment: Baltic/plain grouping is an explicit atlas convention; northern/Urals/Caucasus transitions need physical review.

subcontinents.name: Eastern South America
subcontinents.assessment: Brazil-only partition reflects source political integrity; source-based Amazon/Cerrado/Atlantic regional choices remain open.

subcontinents.name: Indian Ocean Islands
subcontinents.assessment: Western islands plus Chagos; broad oceanic association, not continental adjacency everywhere.

subcontinents.name: Melanesia
subcontinents.assessment: Southwestern Pacific mistakenly adds Polynesian/Micronesian groups; correction required before approval.

subcontinents.name: Mesoamerica
subcontinents.assessment: Atlas uses all Mexico/Central America rather than literal precolonial Mesoamerican cultural extent; terminology must be explained or changed.

subcontinents.name: Micronesia
subcontinents.assessment: Needs Gilbert/Nauru reconciliation without assigning all Kiribati islands by country.

subcontinents.name: Northern Africa
subcontinents.assessment: Mainland North Africa plus Macaronesia; Azores continental association is the highest-priority convention choice.

subcontinents.name: Northern America
subcontinents.assessment: Shared Canada/US groups are country-independent; two one-location residual regions are artifacts.

subcontinents.name: Northern Asia
subcontinents.assessment: Urals, Siberia and Far East boundary convention remains open, with duplicate source area portions.

subcontinents.name: Northern Europe
subcontinents.assessment: Nordic and British/Irish groups are meaningful; Isle of Man is wrongly assigned to Nordic.

subcontinents.name: Northern South America
subcontinents.assessment: A transnational north is defensible but repeats region role and retains border-parent mismatches.

subcontinents.name: Polynesia
subcontinents.assessment: Needs western Polynesian groups currently under Melanesia; Hawaii/Rapa Nui show geographic ownership independence.

subcontinents.name: Southeastern Asia
subcontinents.assessment: Mainland, Malay archipelago and South China Sea groups are mixed with a wrong East China label.

subcontinents.name: Southern Africa
subcontinents.assessment: Southern/south-tropical botanical zones require coherent physical/admin regional roles.

subcontinents.name: Southern Asia
subcontinents.assessment: Indian subcontinent coherent but country/state/botanical areas mix scale and source roles.

subcontinents.name: Southern Europe
subcontinents.assessment: Iberian/Italian/Balkan roles plausible, but Channel Islands and leftover country labels require repair.

subcontinents.name: Southern Ocean Islands
subcontinents.assessment: Artificial Antarctica-exclusion association. Macquarie is not Indian Ocean; ocean-specific region names required.

subcontinents.name: Southern South America
subcontinents.assessment: Broad latitude/administrative grouping encompasses multiple physical regions and southern-ocean archipelagos.

subcontinents.name: Western Africa
subcontinents.assessment: Macro-membership plausible, but country-sized areas and Sahel/coast transitions remain open.

subcontinents.name: Western Asia
subcontinents.assessment: Arabia, Caucasus and residual Western Asia use different geographic scales; boundary conventions remain open.

subcontinents.name: Western Europe
subcontinents.assessment: Central Europe under Western Europe is an atlas macro-convention, not universally agreed geography.

evidence_notes.finding: Papuasia was created on floristic grounds; Cocos moved into Malesia; Andaman/Nicobar moved into Indo-China; Chagos moved into Western Indian Ocean. These explain present inherited groups but do not approve their atlas tier role.

Melanesia rows list Fiji, New Caledonia, PNG, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu. Micronesia includes Kiribati and Nauru; Polynesia includes American Samoa, Cook Islands, Niue, Samoa, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu and Wallis/Futuna. M49 applies by territory and must not override different physical archipelago roles within Kiribati or US minor outlying islands.

Official Bahamas page describes Bimini as islands 50 miles from Florida’s eastern coast; current Biminis→Florida→Southeastern U.S.A. role is misleading. A Bahamas/Caribbean association is a defensible explicit atlas convention.

Confirms named Crown Dependencies and constitutional role only. This source does not establish geographic regional parents; observed polygons and geographic conventions must support Irish Sea/English Channel grouping.

Greenland and Caribbean islands are generally associated with North America; Europe–Asia separation uses a Ural line toward Caspian/Black Seas; expanded Oceania can include Pacific islands. Exact Caucasus watershed and remote ocean islands are not determined by this broad overview.
